claim: A relay operator can bind one managed viewer/editor/admin member to an explicitly supplied Ed25519 installation public key. The exact bundled relay and product provider require a fresh typed proof for every physical connection, deny stale or replayed proofs before retained data, and retain v1-v3 compatibility.
commands: node ../scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- npm exec vitest run src/workspace/relayDeviceEnrollment.test.ts src/workspace/websocketProjectProvider.test.ts src/workspace/websocketProjectProvider.signed.test.ts src/workspace/websocketProjectInvite.test.ts src/workspace/WorkspaceView.ui.test.ts src/components/CollaborationIdentitySettings.ui.test.tsx src/migrations.test.ts
proved: The public enrollment codec validates exact fields, canonical base64url Ed25519 public-key bytes, and a SHA-256-derived key ID; it contains no private key.
The native typed signer binds room ID, member ID, capability generation, issue time, 32-byte nonce, and the exact capability under the syzygy-relay-member-access-v1 domain.
The relay stores the validated public enrollment beside only the capability SHA-256 digest and reports only the public key ID.
A bound member requires six exact query fields, a matching generation, a proof no more than one minute old, no more than 15 seconds of forward skew, and a valid signature from its stored key.
The relay atomically consumes a valid proof in a bounded replay cache before registering the peer or sending retained data.
The product disables y-websocket query reuse after a physical close, destroys that provider, obtains a new native signature, and creates a replacement provider with a new nonce.
Settings exposes a copyable public enrollment request; the relay-host member UI requires it for new members and can retain or replace the binding during exact-revision rotation.
Store v7 and v4 invitations strictly persist only the enrolled key ID with the member credential; v1-v3 invitations remain readable.
notProved: A legal person, organization, email account, or self-reported participant name owns the self-issued installation key.
The shared Yjs device directory or another installation approves the binding; membership authority remains local to the relay operator.
Installation-key backup, escrow, recovery, or in-place rotation. The relay operator can rotate a member credential onto a separately supplied replacement enrollment.
Trusted time. Freshness and capability expiry use the relay host operating-system clock.
Public TLS/WSS operations, automatic invitation delivery, shared/remote administration, signed durable research events, physical packaged two-install interaction, or five-client soak.
